content_units: LMS Shortlist for a 420-Student Secondary School

For a small private secondary school with   420 students, 35 teachers, a modest IT team, and strong sensitivity to recurring cost  , the best overall fit is usually   Google Classroom   for simplicity and low overhead, with   Moodle   as the best low-cost customizable option if the school can handle more setup, and   Canvas   as the strongest polished platform if ease and features matter more than budget.
Moodle vs Google Classroom vs Canvas
Platform   Setup Complexity   Teacher Training Burden   Parent Communication   Assignment Workflows   Grading   Integrations   Likely Fit

Moodle   High   Moderate to High   Moderate with plugins/portal setup   Very flexible; strong for quizzes, modules, deadlines   Strong gradebook, customizable but less intuitive   Extensive via plugins and LTI; highest flexibility   Best for low license cost and customization if IT support is available

Google Classroom   Low   Low   Basic to Moderate; guardian summaries are simple but limited   Very easy for posting, collecting, and returning work   Simple and teacher-friendly, less robust for complex grading   Excellent with Google Workspace; lighter beyond that   Best for modest IT teams and lowest operational burden

Canvas   Moderate   Low to Moderate   Stronger built-in communication and observer/parent options   Polished workflow; consistent submission and feedback tools   Strong, user-friendly gradebook and rubric support   Strong app ecosystem and LTI integrations   Best all-around user experience, but usually higher recurring cost
Best-Fit Recommendation for Your School
1) Recommended: Google Classroom
-   Why it fits:   lowest friction for rollout, minimal admin overhead, fast teacher adoption.
-   Best for:   schools already using Google Workspace for Education.
-   Trade-off:   weaker parent-facing features and less depth in grading, analytics, and course structure than a full LMS.
Explore Classroom
2) Strong low-cost alternative: Moodle
-   Why it fits:   no per-student license in the traditional proprietary sense, highly configurable, academically robust.
-   Best for:   schools willing to invest staff time in setup, hosting, permissions, course templates, and support.
-   Trade-off:   higher implementation complexity and greater dependence on internal or vendor technical help.
Explore Moodle
3) Premium usability option: Canvas
-   Why it fits:   easiest full-feature LMS experience for teachers and students among the three.
-   Best for:   schools that want stronger grading, parent visibility, and consistency across departments.
-   Trade-off:   likely the highest recurring cost, which may conflict with a modest-budget priority.
Explore Canvas
Practical Decision Notes for a Small Private School
If your top priority is lowest ongoing cost
-   Choose Google Classroom   if Google Workspace already covers your core needs.
-   Choose Moodle   if you want more control and can absorb more technical/admin work.
If your top priority is easiest teacher adoption
-   Google Classroom   is usually the fastest to learn.
-   Canvas   is also teacher-friendly, but cost is the main hurdle.
If your top priority is stronger academic structure and grading
-   Canvas   offers the most polished grading and workflow experience.
-   Moodle   is powerful, but less intuitive without careful setup and training.
If your top priority is parent communication
-   Canvas   is strongest out of the box.
-   Google Classroom   works for simple guardian summaries, but is not a full parent-engagement system.
-   Moodle   can support parent access, but this often requires more configuration.
School Context Applied
For a school of   420 students and 35 teachers  , the platform should minimize:
- admin time spent on account management and troubleshooting
- teacher retraining across departments
- recurring costs that scale poorly
- dependence on a large internal IT team
That points to this ranking for your stated priorities:
1.   Google Classroom   — best overall fit for simplicity + low recurring cost
2.   Moodle   — best if low license cost matters most and the school accepts higher setup/admin effort
3.   Canvas   — best product experience, but usually hardest to justify on budget for this profile
